claims.text: The deviation is established on the trace. The GPS polyline runs 16.2 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff against a platform optimal of 12.0 km — an excess of 4.2 km, or 35% of the optimal. Under POL-RD-01 both establishment tests pass: the excess is more than 0.8 km in absolute terms AND more than 20% of the optimal distance. Neither limb is marginal on this record.

The distance figure the threshold must be measured on is the trace figure: POL-RD-01 provides that where gps_trace.trace_distance_km and trip_record.actual_distance_km disagree, the trace governs, because the trip record is a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement. Here trace_distance_km is 16.2 km, and that is the figure carried into the excess computation, so the finding is safe on the clause's own terms.

The trace is NOT impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07. It carries 205 fixes at a 10 second sample interval with coverage_pct 100.0, max_gap_sec 0.0 and an empty gaps array, so none of limbs (a) to (c) is met — no gap over 90 seconds, no straight-line jump over 500 m, no sustained sampling interval above 30 seconds. The deviation may therefore be established on the trace alone, and no corroboration requirement under POL-RD-07(ii) bites.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged. The same trip identifier TRP-09111 appears on the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown, and the trace opens at 2026-09-18T08:05:00+08:00 which is the trip's recorded start, so limb (a) — that the artifacts describe the same trip — is satisfied. Limb (b) is satisfied because the excess exceeds the POL-RD-01 threshold on an unimpaired trace. Further, rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0, so POL-RD-08's additional-corroboration proviso for repeat claimants is not engaged at all.

No traffic advisory exonerates any of the excess. EV-ADVIS-09111-01 is the only advisory in the bundle and it carries no payload, so there is on this record no named road, expressway segment or junction for POL-RD-03 to work on, no validity window, and nothing to match against a departure from and rejoinder to the optimal corridor. Absence is citable: the record contains no advisory covering this road.

No part of the excess is exonerated as rider-requested. The chat log holds exactly two messages: at 08:12:00 the rider wrote that the route was left after Pioneer Road and asked the driver to return to the booked route, and at 08:12:35 the driver replied only that he was following the road ahead. Neither message carries a waypoint_hint, and the driver names no road. Under POL-RD-04 the instruction must come from the rider, be timely, and identify an actable place or road with the trace passing within 200 m of the requested waypoint — here there is no rider detour request at all, so the clause is unavailable and the excess is not reduced by it.

No endpoint amendment re-quotes the optimal route. POL-RD-05 requires amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min where a pickup or dropoff point was moved after booking, and both fields are null; pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are likewise null and original_pickup and original_dropoff are null. The clause therefore re-applies POL-RD-01 against nothing and excuses nothing.

The refund route is open because the fare is metered, not quoted. fare_breakdown.fare_model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so the distance and time charges were not fixed at booking. POL-RD-11, which closes the distance-refund route, is confined to UPFRONT_QUOTE trips and does not apply, and POL-RD-02 accordingly runs against the booked optimal route of 12.0 km and 24.0 minutes.

The POL-RD-02 arithmetic is this. Charged total is SGD 33.36. The recomputed fare is ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 12.0 optimal km + 0.28 x 24.0 optimal min) x 1.2 surge, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 for the on-optimal-route Pioneer Road inbound gantry - 1.00 promo discount = SGD 24.2240. The refund is 33.36 - 24.2240 = SGD 9.1360 before rounding. Intermediate values are not rounded; the payable figure rounds UP to the nearest SGD 0.05, giving SGD 9.15.

The refund is a partial refund, not a full one, and it is still the whole of what the rider asks. The refund is 27.4% of the charged total, far below the 90% share POL-RD-02 sets as the trigger for a full refund, so the outcome is a partial refund of SGD 9.15. That figure is exactly the amount the rider contests, so the rider is made good on the entire sum in dispute and claims nothing beyond it.

The off-route ERP is already inside that refund and is NOT added on top. The fare breakdown charges SGD 3.00 in ERP: SGD 1.00 for the on-optimal-route Pioneer Road inbound gantry and SGD 2.00 for the Tuas South Avenue 8 loop gantry, which is off the optimal route. POL-RD-09(1) provides that off-route ERP is comprehended in the POL-RD-02 refund because the recomputed fare includes only on-optimal-route gantries; such lines are itemised for transparency but must never be added again. The rider therefore claims SGD 9.15 and no more rather than doubling the pass-through.

The rider's claim is corroborated independently of the trace, so it does not stand on the GPS alone. The rider's own contemporaneous message at 08:12:00 records that the route was left after Pioneer Road, and the fare breakdown charges a gantry that is off the optimal route, which places the vehicle on a corridor the optimal route does not use. Both artifacts are independent of the trace under POL-RD-07(ii), and both are consistent with the 4.2 km excess.

claims.text: The excess measured on the governing trace is 4.2 km, which is 35.0% of the 12.0 km optimal route (EV-GPS-09111, derived.deviation.excess_km and excess_pct). On this trip's own trace both POL-RD-01 establishment gates are met, but the excess falls below BOTH materiality gates in that same clause - it is not greater than 50% of optimal and not greater than 8.0 km absolute - so this is not a MATERIAL deviation. The consequence matters: POL-RD-06 is engaged only 'whenever POL-RD-01 records a MATERIAL deviation', so the driver-profile uplift and the conduct referral cannot attach to this trip.

No repeat-deviation pattern is established on the two fields POL-RD-06 and POL-GEN-01 permit for that test. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 610 (EV-DPROF-09111): the count is below 3 and the ratio (0/610) is far below 0.05, so limb (b) of POL-RD-06 does not fire, no FULL_REFUND uplift is available to the rider, and no driver-conduct referral under POL-RD-06(c) is warranted. POL-GEN-01 confines this test to those two fields; the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags (also 0) is context only and may not be substituted for the trailing-90-day figure.

The Tuas South Avenue 8 loop ERP line of SGD 2.00 is off-optimal-route ERP (on_optimal_route false on EV-FARE-09111), and off-route ERP is already comprehended inside any POL-RD-02 recomputation: the recomputed fare is rebuilt on the optimal route and includes only the SGD 1.00 on-route gantry. Under POL-RD-09(1) that SGD 2.00 is itemised in the ruling for transparency but must NEVER be added on top of the POL-RD-02 figure - the rider's complaint about an 'extra ERP charge' is answered inside the single distance-and-time refund, not by a second, additive payment.

The Pioneer Road inbound gantry of SGD 1.00 lies on the optimal route (on_optimal_route true, EV-FARE-09111) and is a government-set pass-through properly chargeable to the rider; it correctly remains inside the recomputed fare and therefore reduces any refund, and as a pass-through line it is not multiplied by the 1.2 surge on the fare_breakdown. The ERP ledger total on this fare is SGD 3.00, of which only the on-route SGD 1.00 may sit in the recomputed fare.

On this record the rider's recovery is capped by the POL-RD-02 arithmetic and nothing larger is available. charged_total is 33.36 and recomputed_fare is ((3.80 + 0.75 x 12.0 + 0.28 x 24.0) x 1.2 surge read from the fare_breakdown) + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 on-route ERP - 1.00 promo = 24.224 (EV-FARE-09111), giving 33.36 - 24.224 = 9.136, rounded up to SGD 9.15. That refund is 27.4% of charged_total, far below the 90% full-refund share, so even on the rider's best case the outcome is at most a PARTIAL_REFUND, and at SGD 9.15 it is plainly above the SGD 0.50 de minimis. No larger, and no discretionary, sum is supportable.

ruling.explanation:
Rider and driver — this is the decision on trip TRP-09111.

The trip was longer than booked, and part of what was charged is refundable. I measured the deviation on the GPS trace, not the trip record: POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure the governing one, and here the trace is 16.2 km against a platform optimal of 12.0 km — an excess of 4.2 km, or 35%. That clears both establishment tests (more than 20% of optimal and more than 0.8 km). I also checked the trace's integrity: 205 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage and no gaps, so it is not impaired for policy purposes and the deviation stands on the trace alone.

The excess is not, however, a material deviation: 35% is below 50% and 4.2 km is below 8.0 km, so POL-RD-06 is not engaged — no full-refund uplift and no driver-conduct referral. The driver's 90-day deviation flags are 0 against 610 completed trips. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is context only under POL-GEN-01 and was not used for any test.

Nothing excuses the excess. The only traffic advisory on the record carries no content, so POL-RD-03 cannot apply. The chat log shows no rider detour request — the rider's 08:12 message asked the driver to rejoin the booked route — so POL-RD-04 does not reduce the excess. No pickup or dropoff was amended, so POL-RD-05 does not apply. The driver's statement that he followed the road available cites no artifact; under POL-RD-08 a general assertion about road conditions does not discharge the driver's burden.

The fare is metered and has no quoted price, so POL-RD-11 does not apply and the refund is the POL-RD-02 arithmetic: charged total 33.36 less a recomputed fare of ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 12.0 km + 0.28 x 24.0 min) x 1.2 surge, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 on-route ERP − 1.00 promo = 24.224; the difference is 9.136, rounded up to SGD 9.15. At 27.4% of the charged total that is below the 90% full-refund share and above the 0.50 de minimis, so the outcome is a partial refund of SGD 9.15 — the sum contested.

On the ERP point raised by the rider: the 2.00 Tuas South Avenue 8 loop gantry is off the optimal route and is already comprehended inside the 9.15 (POL-RD-09(1)); it is itemised for transparency but is not added a second time. The 1.00 Pioneer Road gantry lies on the optimal route, correctly remains in the recomputed fare, and as a pass-through line is not multiplied by the 1.2 surge.

No escalation trigger applies: the trip identifiers match across all artifacts, the trace is clean, the timestamps agree, and the refund is far below any ceiling. No clause produces a referral. Rider: SGD 9.15 is refunded. Driver: the balance of the fare stands and no compensation is due.

To both parties: this is a metered RYDE_X trip (TRP-09111, 18 Sep 2026). The same trip identifier appears on the trip record, GPS trace and fare breakdown, and the trace opens at the recorded start time, so the artifacts describe this trip.

THE DEVIATION IS ESTABLISHED, BUT NOT MATERIAL. The governing figure is the trace length, not the trip record's rounded copy: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 16.2 km (EV-GPS-09111) against the booking-time optimal of 12.0 km (EV-TRIP-09111), an excess of 4.2 km = 35% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 establishment gates (over 0.8 km and over 20%) pass. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes: 205 fixes at a 10-second interval, coverage 100%, no gaps, no jump over 500 m and no sampling interval over 30 s, so POL-RD-07 does not bite and the finding may rest on the trace alone. Materiality, however, requires an excess over 50% of optimal or over 8.0 km; at 35% and 4.2 km neither is met, so POL-RD-06 is NOT engaged and no driver_profile check, FULL_REFUND uplift or conduct referral attaches (I record that the profile shows deviation_flags_90d 0 against 610 completed trips, and that the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is context only under POL-GEN-01 and was not used).

THE REFUND IS ARITHMETIC (POL-RD-02; the fare is METERED with a null quoted fare, so POL-RD-11 does not apply). charged_total = SGD 33.36. recomputed_fare = ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 12.0 km + 0.28 x 24.0 min) x 1.2 surge, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 for the on-optimal-route Pioneer Road inbound gantry - 1.00 promo = SGD 24.2240. Refund = 33.36 - 24.2240 = SGD 9.1360, rounded UP to SGD 9.15. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis, and it is 27.4% of the charge, far below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is a partial refund and not a full one. The figure equals the amount you contested, rider.

THE 'EXTRA ERP' IS ANSWERED INSIDE THAT FIGURE, NOT ON TOP OF IT. The fare's SGD 3.00 of ERP is the SGD 1.00 Pioneer Road inbound gantry (on the optimal route and properly chargeable) plus the SGD 2.00 Tuas South Avenue 8 loop gantry (off the optimal route). The recomputed fare already rebuilds the trip without the off-route gantry, so that SGD 2.00 is comprehended in the SGD 9.15 and must never be added again (POL-RD-09(1)); the on-route gantry correctly stays in.

NOTHING REDUCES OR EXCUSES THE EXCESS. There is no rider-requested detour: the chat log contains only the rider asking the driver to return to the booked route and the driver naming no actable road, and no message carries a waypoint_hint, so POL-RD-04 is unavailable. No endpoint was amended (the amended fields are null), so POL-RD-05 excuses nothing. The only traffic advisory in the bundle (EV-ADVIS-09111-01) carries no payload, so POL-RD-03 exonerates nothing. The driver's statement that he 'followed the road available to me' is a general assertion citing no artifact and no clause, and carries no weight under POL-RD-08; on the record the excess stands unexplained.

No referral is made. No repeat-deviation pattern is established (so POL-RD-06(c) does not fire), and the off-route ERP is a pass-through item comprehended in the distance refund rather than a billing-integrity defect requiring a POL-RD-09(4) reference. ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this is trip TRP-09111, a metered fare, and the outcome is fixed by the policy arithmetic rather than by discretion.

ROUTE. The governing distance is the GPS trace: it runs 16.2 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff against a platform optimal of 12.0 km. POL-RD-01 provides that where gps_trace.trace_distance_km and trip_record.actual_distance_km disagree the trace governs; the trip record's 16.2 km is a rounded copy of the same measurement and cannot be used for the threshold test. The excess is 4.2 km, or 35.0% of optimal. That passes both establishment gates (more than 0.8 km and more than 20%), so a deviation is established. It passes neither materiality gate (more than 50% or more than 8.0 km), so the POL-RD-06 driver-profile review is not triggered; in any event the only fields POL-RD-06 and POL-GEN-01 permit for that test show no pattern (deviation_flags_90d 0 against completed_trips_90d 610), and the lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is context only.

EXONERATION. None applies. The only traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-09111-01) carries no payload, so POL-RD-03 has no named road, validity window or alternative route to work on and exonerates nothing. The chat log (EV-CHAT-09111) shows the rider asking the driver to return to the booked route at 08:12, with no waypoint and no rider instruction to detour, so POL-RD-04 does not reduce the excess (and your counterparty statement that no stop was requested is consistent with that). No pickup or dropoff was amended and no amended optimal exists, so POL-RD-05 does not apply. The fare is METERED with quoted_fare_sgd null, so POL-RD-11's bar on distance refunds does not apply and POL-RD-02 runs.

REFUND. Charged total is 33.36. The recomputed fare is ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 12.0 optimal km + 0.28 x 24.0 optimal min) x the 1.2 surge read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 for the on-optimal-route Pioneer Road inbound gantry - 1.00 promo = 24.2240. The refund is 33.36 - 24.2240 = 9.1360, rounded up to SGD 9.15. That is 27.4% of the charge, below the 90% full-refund share, and above the SGD 0.50 de minimis: PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 9.15, which is the whole of the amount contested.

THE EXTRA ERP. The fare carries 3.00 of ERP. The 1.00 Pioneer Road inbound gantry lies on the optimal route (the trip record carries it as optimal_route_erp_sgd) and is properly chargeable, so it stays inside the recomputed fare. The 2.00 Tuas South Avenue 8 loop line is off the optimal route and, on the trace, no fix comes within the 250 m match radius of that gantry (nearest fix 1,645.7 m), so the vehicle never passed it; that is a billing-integrity defect recorded for review. The money is not doubled: POL-RD-09(1) provides that off-route ERP is already comprehended in the POL-RD-02 figure and must never be added on top, so the 2.00 is returned inside the 9.15 and is not paid a second time.

EVIDENCE WEIGHT. The facts that decide the case - the excess and the refund - are carried by the GPS trace, the trip record and the fare breakdown, none of which is impaired. The trace is clean for policy purposes (205 fixes at a 10 s interval, no gap, full coverage), so POL-RD-07 corroboration is not required and the rider's extra corroboration point is moot. The ruling is therefore not capped below the platform floor.
referrals: POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity review: the SGD 2.00 'Tuas South Avenue 8 loop' ERP line is charged although no GPS fix lies within the 250 m gantry-match radius (nearest fix 1,645.7 m) - a gantry the vehicle never passed.

ruling.explanation:
Rider, your claim is upheld in the amount you contested, SGD 9.15. Driver, the excess is established on your own trip's trace, but no conduct finding attaches to you and no compensation is due to you.

Deviation (POL-RD-01). The governing distance is the trace figure. The GPS polyline runs 16.2 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff (EV-GPS-09111, trace_distance_km 16.2) against a platform optimal of 12.0 km (EV-TRIP-09111). Excess = 4.2 km, or 35.0% of optimal. Both establishment gates pass (more than 0.8 km absolute AND more than 20% of optimal), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED. It is NOT material — 35% is below the 50% gate and 4.2 km is below the 8.0 km gate — so the POL-RD-06 driver-profile uplift and the POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral cannot attach, and neither does.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes (POL-RD-07): 205 fixes at a 10-second interval, coverage_pct 100.0, max_gap_sec 0.0 and an empty gaps array, so none of limbs (a)–(c) is met, and no corroboration requirement bites.

No clause excuses the excess. EV-ADVIS-09111-01 carries no payload, so no traffic advisory names a road, window or corridor for POL-RD-03 to work on. The two chat messages (08:12:00 rider / 08:12:35 driver, EV-CHAT-09111) contain no rider detour request, no waypoint_hint and no named road, so POL-RD-04 is unavailable. Both amended_optimal fields and both amendment timestamps are null, so POL-RD-05 re-quotes nothing (EV-TRIP-09111). The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged: TRP-09111 matches across the trip record, trace and fare breakdown, and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0, so the repeat-claimant proviso is not engaged.

Refund (POL-RD-02, metered fare — fare_model METERED and quoted_fare_sgd null, so POL-RD-11 does not apply). Charged_total = SGD 33.36. Recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 × 12.0 + 0.28 × 24.0) × 1.2 surge read from EV-FARE-09111) + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 on-optimal-route ERP − 1.00 promo = SGD 24.2240. Refund = 33.36 − 24.2240 = SGD 9.1360, which rounds UP to SGD 9.15. That is 27.4% of charged_total, well below the 90% full-refund share, and far above the SGD 0.50 de minimis, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 9.15.

ERP (POL-RD-09). The SGD 3.00 of ERP splits into SGD 1.00 for the Pioneer Road inbound gantry, which lies on the optimal route and is properly chargeable, and SGD 2.00 for the Tuas South Avenue 8 loop gantry, which is off the optimal route. Under POL-RD-09(1) the off-route SGD 2.00 is already comprehended in the recomputed fare (which includes only on-route gantries) and is itemised for transparency but never added on top. Separately, the trace's closest approach to the Tuas South Avenue 8 gantry is 1,645.7 m (EV-GPS-09111), far beyond the 250 m match radius, so the trace never passes it: that is a billing-integrity defect under POL-RD-09(4) and is recorded as a referral. Because it is refunded under that limb, POL-RD-10(8) is not triggered and this does not escalate the case.

No repeat-deviation pattern: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 610 (EV-DPROF-09111), so no POL-RD-06 uplift or conduct referral. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is context-only under POL-GEN-01 and was not used; the referee flagged its mention and it carries no weight.

Confidence is 0.90. Every artifact carrying a deciding fact — the GPS trace, the trip record and the fare breakdown — sits at full weight, and the ruling is well above the 0.70 escalation floor, so no escalation is required.
referrals: POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity: the SGD 2.00 Tuas South Avenue 8 loop ERP line charges a gantry the GPS trace never passes (nearest fix 1,645.7 m, beyond the 250 m match radius) — record the billing-integrity finding. The sum is already comprehended in the POL-RD-02 recomputation, so nothing is added on top of the refund.

flags.claim: No repeat-deviation pattern is established on the two fields POL-RD-06 and POL-GEN-01 permit for that test. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 610 (EV-DPROF-09111): the count is below 3 and the ratio (0/610) is far below 0.05, so limb (b) of POL-RD-06 does not fire, no FULL_REFUND uplift is available to the rider, and no driver-conduct referral under POL-RD-06(c) is warranted. POL-GEN-01 confines this test to those two fields; the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags (also 0) is context only and may not be substituted for the trailing-90-day figure.

ledger.claim: The deviation is established on the trace. The GPS polyline runs 16.2 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff against a platform optimal of 12.0 km — an excess of 4.2 km, or 35% of the optimal. Under POL-RD-01 both establishment tests pass: the excess is more than 0.8 km in absolute terms AND more than 20% of the optimal distance. Neither limb is marginal on this record.

The distance figure the threshold must be measured on is the trace figure: POL-RD-01 provides that where gps_trace.trace_distance_km and trip_record.actual_distance_km disagree, the trace governs, because the trip record is a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement. Here trace_distance_km is 16.2 km, and that is the figure carried into the excess computation, so the finding is safe on the clause's own terms.

The trace is NOT impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07. It carries 205 fixes at a 10 second sample interval with coverage_pct 100.0, max_gap_sec 0.0 and an empty gaps array, so none of limbs (a) to (c) is met — no gap over 90 seconds, no straight-line jump over 500 m, no sustained sampling interval above 30 seconds. The deviation may therefore be established on the trace alone, and no corroboration requirement under POL-RD-07(ii) bites.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged. The same trip identifier TRP-09111 appears on the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown, and the trace opens at 2026-09-18T08:05:00+08:00 which is the trip's recorded start, so limb (a) — that the artifacts describe the same trip — is satisfied. Limb (b) is satisfied because the excess exceeds the POL-RD-01 threshold on an unimpaired trace. Further, rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0, so POL-RD-08's additional-corroboration proviso for repeat claimants is not engaged at all.

No traffic advisory exonerates any of the excess. EV-ADVIS-09111-01 is the only advisory in the bundle and it carries no payload, so there is on this record no named road, expressway segment or junction for POL-RD-03 to work on, no validity window, and nothing to match against a departure from and rejoinder to the optimal corridor. Absence is citable: the record contains no advisory covering this road.

No part of the excess is exonerated as rider-requested. The chat log holds exactly two messages: at 08:12:00 the rider wrote that the route was left after Pioneer Road and asked the driver to return to the booked route, and at 08:12:35 the driver replied only that he was following the road ahead. Neither message carries a waypoint_hint, and the driver names no road. Under POL-RD-04 the instruction must come from the rider, be timely, and identify an actable place or road with the trace passing within 200 m of the requested waypoint — here there is no rider detour request at all, so the clause is unavailable and the excess is not reduced by it.

No endpoint amendment re-quotes the optimal route. POL-RD-05 requires amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min where a pickup or dropoff point was moved after booking, and both fields are null; pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are likewise null and original_pickup and original_dropoff are null. The clause therefore re-applies POL-RD-01 against nothing and excuses nothing.

The refund route is open because the fare is metered, not quoted. fare_breakdown.fare_model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so the distance and time charges were not fixed at booking. POL-RD-11, which closes the distance-refund route, is confined to UPFRONT_QUOTE trips and does not apply, and POL-RD-02 accordingly runs against the booked optimal route of 12.0 km and 24.0 minutes.

The POL-RD-02 arithmetic is this. Charged total is SGD 33.36. The recomputed fare is ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 12.0 optimal km + 0.28 x 24.0 optimal min) x 1.2 surge, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 for the on-optimal-route Pioneer Road inbound gantry - 1.00 promo discount = SGD 24.2240. The refund is 33.36 - 24.2240 = SGD 9.1360 before rounding. Intermediate values are not rounded; the payable figure rounds UP to the nearest SGD 0.05, giving SGD 9.15.

The refund is a partial refund, not a full one, and it is still the whole of what the rider asks. The refund is 27.4% of the charged total, far below the 90% share POL-RD-02 sets as the trigger for a full refund, so the outcome is a partial refund of SGD 9.15. That figure is exactly the amount the rider contests, so the rider is made good on the entire sum in dispute and claims nothing beyond it.

The off-route ERP is already inside that refund and is NOT added on top. The fare breakdown charges SGD 3.00 in ERP: SGD 1.00 for the on-optimal-route Pioneer Road inbound gantry and SGD 2.00 for the Tuas South Avenue 8 loop gantry, which is off the optimal route. POL-RD-09(1) provides that off-route ERP is comprehended in the POL-RD-02 refund because the recomputed fare includes only on-optimal-route gantries; such lines are itemised for transparency but must never be added again. The rider therefore claims SGD 9.15 and no more rather than doubling the pass-through.

The rider's claim is corroborated independently of the trace, so it does not stand on the GPS alone. The rider's own contemporaneous message at 08:12:00 records that the route was left after Pioneer Road, and the fare breakdown charges a gantry that is off the optimal route, which places the vehicle on a corridor the optimal route does not use. Both artifacts are independent of the trace under POL-RD-07(ii), and both are consistent with the 4.2 km excess.

The excess measured on the governing trace is 4.2 km, which is 35.0% of the 12.0 km optimal route (EV-GPS-09111, derived.deviation.excess_km and excess_pct). On this trip's own trace both POL-RD-01 establishment gates are met, but the excess falls below BOTH materiality gates in that same clause - it is not greater than 50% of optimal and not greater than 8.0 km absolute - so this is not a MATERIAL deviation. The consequence matters: POL-RD-06 is engaged only 'whenever POL-RD-01 records a MATERIAL deviation', so the driver-profile uplift and the conduct referral cannot attach to this trip.

No repeat-deviation pattern is established on the two fields POL-RD-06 and POL-GEN-01 permit for that test. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 610 (EV-DPROF-09111): the count is below 3 and the ratio (0/610) is far below 0.05, so limb (b) of POL-RD-06 does not fire, no FULL_REFUND uplift is available to the rider, and no driver-conduct referral under POL-RD-06(c) is warranted. POL-GEN-01 confines this test to those two fields; the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags (also 0) is context only and may not be substituted for the trailing-90-day figure.

ledger.claim: The Tuas South Avenue 8 loop ERP line of SGD 2.00 is off-optimal-route ERP (on_optimal_route false on EV-FARE-09111), and off-route ERP is already comprehended inside any POL-RD-02 recomputation: the recomputed fare is rebuilt on the optimal route and includes only the SGD 1.00 on-route gantry. Under POL-RD-09(1) that SGD 2.00 is itemised in the ruling for transparency but must NEVER be added on top of the POL-RD-02 figure - the rider's complaint about an 'extra ERP charge' is answered inside the single distance-and-time refund, not by a second, additive payment.

The Pioneer Road inbound gantry of SGD 1.00 lies on the optimal route (on_optimal_route true, EV-FARE-09111) and is a government-set pass-through properly chargeable to the rider; it correctly remains inside the recomputed fare and therefore reduces any refund, and as a pass-through line it is not multiplied by the 1.2 surge on the fare_breakdown. The ERP ledger total on this fare is SGD 3.00, of which only the on-route SGD 1.00 may sit in the recomputed fare.

On this record the rider's recovery is capped by the POL-RD-02 arithmetic and nothing larger is available. charged_total is 33.36 and recomputed_fare is ((3.80 + 0.75 x 12.0 + 0.28 x 24.0) x 1.2 surge read from the fare_breakdown) + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 on-route ERP - 1.00 promo = 24.224 (EV-FARE-09111), giving 33.36 - 24.224 = 9.136, rounded up to SGD 9.15. That refund is 27.4% of charged_total, far below the 90% full-refund share, so even on the rider's best case the outcome is at most a PARTIAL_REFUND, and at SGD 9.15 it is plainly above the SGD 0.50 de minimis. No larger, and no discretionary, sum is supportable.
